say.en: Left hand, right hand. Your two hands are mirror images, yet you cannot place one exactly on the other. Molecules can be like that too, and SN1 and SN2 treat such molecules differently. In this lesson: Identify chiral molecules and enantiomers.
Relate SN2 to inversion and SN1 to racemisation.

body.en: A carbon with four different groups is chiral (asymmetric); its molecule is not superimposable on its mirror image. The two mirror-image forms are enantiomers: they rotate plane-polarised light equally but in opposite directions (dextro, +; laevo, −). An equal mixture of both is a racemic mixture and shows zero rotation.
body.kn: ನಾಲ್ಕು ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಗುಂಪುಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿರುವ ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಅಣುವನ್ನು ಕೈರಲ್ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದರ ಎರಡು ಪ್ರತಿಬಿಂಬ ರೂಪಗಳು ಸಮತಲ ಧ್ರುವೀಕೃತ ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ತಿರುಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ಸಮ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದ ಮಿಶ್ರಣ (ರೇಸಿಮಿಕ್) ತಿರುಗಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

body.en: Heating a haloalkane with alcoholic KOH removes H from the β-carbon and X from the α-carbon, forming an alkene (dehydrohalogenation). When more than one alkene can form, the more substituted alkene is the major product (Zaitsev’s rule). Aqueous KOH favours substitution (alcohol); alcoholic KOH favours *elimination* (alkene).

body.en: Grignard reagent: $R-X + Mg \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R-MgX$. The C–Mg bond is very polar, so R behaves as a carbanion; with any proton source, $RMgX + H_2O \rightarrow RH + Mg(OH)X$. Wurtz reaction: $2R-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R-R + 2NaX$, giving an alkane with double the carbon atoms.

heading.en: Elimination, Metals, Haloarenes and Polyhalogen Compounds

tagline.en: Dehydrohalogenation and Saytzeff's rule, Grignard and Wurtz reactions, why aryl halides resist substitution, their electrophilic substitution, and the uses and hazards of polyhalogen compounds.

myth.en: A nitro group anywhere on the ring makes chlorobenzene easier to hydrolyse.

truth.en: Only nitro groups ortho or para to the halogen activate it strongly. A meta nitro group has almost no such effect. When OH⁻ adds to the carbon carrying Cl, a negative charge spreads to the carbons ortho and para to that position. A nitro group sitting there can pull the charge onto its own oxygens and stabilise the intermediate; from the meta position it cannot.

narration.en: Many people think: A nitro group anywhere on the ring makes chlorobenzene easier to hydrolyse. Actually: Only nitro groups ortho or para to the halogen activate it strongly. A meta nitro group has almost no such effect. When OH⁻ adds to the carbon carrying Cl, a negative charge spreads to the carbons ortho and para to that position. A nitro group sitting there can pull the charge onto its own oxygens and stabilise the intermediate; from the meta position it cannot.

problem.en: What mass of ethane is formed when 19 g of bromomethane reacts completely with sodium in dry ether? (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80)

steps.en: Molar mass of CH₃Br = 12 + 3 + 80 = 95 g/mol; 19 g = 0.2 mol.
0.2 mol CH₃Br gives 0.1 mol C₂H₆; mass = 0.1 × 30 = 3.0 g.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of ethane is formed when 19 g of bromomethane reacts completely with sodium in dry ether? (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80)

say.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of ethane is formed when 19 grams of bromomethane reacts completely with sodium in dry ether? (C equals 12, H equals 1, Br equals 80).
2 CH 3Br plus 2 Na gives C 2H 6 plus 2 NaBr.
Molar mass of CH 3Br equals 12 plus 3 plus 80 equals 95 grams per mole; 19 grams equals 0.2 moles.
0.2 moles CH 3Br gives 0.1 moles C 2H 6; mass equals 0.1 times 30 equals 3.0 grams.
So the answer is 3.0 grams of ethane.

problem.en: Which of 2-chloropropane and 2-chlorobutane is chiral? What happens to its optical activity in an SN1 hydrolysis?

steps.en: 2-Chloropropane: C-2 has H, Cl and two identical CH₃ groups, so it is achiral.
2-Chlorobutane: C-2 has H, Cl, CH₃ and C₂H₅, four different groups, so it is chiral.
SN1 goes through a planar carbocation attacked from both faces, so the butan-2-ol formed is (largely) racemic.

answer.en: 2-Chlorobutane is chiral; SN1 hydrolysis gives a racemic (optically inactive) product

say.en: Let us solve this together. Which of 2-chloropropane and 2-chlorobutane is chiral? What happens to its optical activity in an SN1 hydrolysis?
2-Chloropropane: C-2 has H, Cl and two identical CH 3 groups, so it is achiral.
2-Chlorobutane: C-2 has H, Cl, CH 3 and C 2H 5, four different groups, so it is chiral.
SN1 goes through a planar carbocation attacked from both faces, so the butan-2-ol formed is largely racemic.
So the answer is 2-Chlorobutane is chiral; SN1 hydrolysis gives a racemic optically inactive product.

homework.en: Predict the major alkene from 2-bromo-2-methylbutane with alcoholic KOH.

narration.en: Recap. A carbon with four different groups is chiral; enantiomers rotate light in opposite directions. SN2 inverts configuration; SN1 racemises. Alcoholic KOH eliminates; the more substituted alkene is major (Zaitsev). Grignard reagents need dry ether; Wurtz joins two alkyl groups with Na.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ನಾಲ್ಕು ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಗುಂಪುಗಳಿರುವ ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಕೈರಲ್; ಎನ್ಯಾಂಟಿಯೋಮರ್‌ಗಳು ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ತಿರುಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. SN2 ವಿನ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನು ತಲೆಕೆಳಗು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; SN1 ರೇಸಿಮೀಕರಣ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಆಲ್ಕೋಹಾಲೀಯ KOH ನಿರ್ಮೂಲನ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಆದೇಶಿತ ಆಲ್ಕೀನ್ ಮುಖ್ಯ (ಜೈಟ್ಸೆಫ್). ಗ್ರಿಗ್ನಾರ್ಡ್ ಕಾರಕಕ್ಕೆ ಒಣ ಈಥರ್ ಬೇಕು; ವುರ್ಟ್ಜ್ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ Na ಮೂಲಕ ಎರಡು ಆಲ್ಕೈಲ್ ಗುಂಪುಗಳನ್ನು ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.
